context: Tests the boundary between generic hooks and nativeHooks. Claude Code's Notification event and idle_prompt matcher are agent-specific, so the plugin should use the native escape hatch, keep the entrypoint in the package, and explain why a generic Tessl event is insufficient.

checklist.name: Native hook tier selected
checklist.description: claude-idle-notifier/.tessl-plugin/plugin.json contains top-level `nativeHooks` keyed by the recognized agent id `claude-code`

checklist.name: Agent-specific event represented
checklist.description: The claude-code native hook configuration declares the `Notification` event and filters it for `idle_prompt` using the native shape

checklist.name: Bundled entrypoint anchored
checklist.description: The native hook command references hooks/notify-idle.sh through the exact braced `${TESSL_PLUGIN_DIR}` token rather than a bare relative path

checklist.name: Hook entrypoint ships
checklist.description: A substantive claude-idle-notifier/hooks/notify-idle.sh file exists and is the file referenced by the manifest

checklist.name: Native boundary justified
checklist.description: hook-decision.md explains that `nativeHooks` is necessary because Notification and idle_prompt are Claude Code-specific and are not expressible by the generic PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart, or Stop events

checklist.name: No false generic workaround
checklist.description: The manifest does not incorrectly map the native Notification requirement onto a generic Tessl event or add an unrelated generic hook

checklist.name: No direct Claude config edit
checklist.description: The output does not create or edit .claude/settings.json; Tessl is left to materialize the native hook on install

checklist.name: Valid plugin metadata
checklist.description: claude-idle-notifier/.tessl-plugin/plugin.json has the requested name plus valid version and description fields
